sentence: The decisive factor is [RF58B7]: Broadcom's announced $70–100B AI financing debt will materially worsen leverage within months, counteracting FY2025's deleveraging recovery and creating near-term financial risk.

[C:operating-income-rebound] is substantial, but the bear correctly identifies that [C:vware-amort-rolloff] contributed materially to the improvement.

On SBC, the bear's concern about [C:sbc-permanent-earnings-drag] is structurally valid; absolute cash dilution rose from $2.2B to $7.6B, a permanent increase in equity grants.

The crux is financing debt: [C:debt-financing-explicit] confirms new debt issuance, but whether this appears as corporate leverage or off-balance-sheet securitization determines whether [C:leverage-risk-incoming-debt] is imminent or manageable.

[C:fcf-negative-operating-leverage] is arithmetically correct—FY2025 FCF on a 78% larger revenue base is nearly flat—but the bull's point that [C:fcf-conversion-capex-driven] reflects mix shift and capex, not earnings erosion, is plausible if VMware integration capex normalizes.

The bull's case is stronger on core operational trends ([C:segment-organic-growth] and margin expansion within segments), while the bear's case is stronger on balance-sheet risk trajectory if AI financing debt is indeed $70–100B of new corporate leverage.
